astronomy_picture_of_the_day.title: Venus and Jupiter: Conjunction from Avebury
astronomy_picture_of_the_day.explanation: To see Venus and Jupiter together this month, you won't need binoculars or even a telescope. Just look up after sunset and you'll find them emerging as the sky grows dark near the western horizon. In fact, on June 9 the two brightest planets were in close conjunction, separated on the sky by less than 2 degrees from our perspective.
